title: Covariance-Aware BAO Consistency Test of Energy-Flow Cosmology Using the BOSS DR12 Consensus Likelihood
description: This research note tests the Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) modified background expansion against precision BAO data using the official BOSS DR12 consensus likelihood with the full 6×6 covariance matrix. With DESI DR2-calibrated EFC parameters held fixed (no refitting), EFC attains a modest improvement over ΛCDM (Δχ² ≈ −2.36) and passes a stringent, reproducible covariance-aware BAO consistency test; results are cross-checked with cosmic chronometer H(z) data.

key_results.main_finding: With parameters fixed to DESI DR2-calibrated values, EFC achieves a modest improvement over ΛCDM on BOSS DR12 BAO with full covariance and passes this stringent consistency test without parameter retuning.
datasets_used: BOSS DR12 consensus BAO (DM,H at z = 0.38, 0.51, 0.61; full 6×6 covariance; rs_fid = 147.78 Mpc)
Cosmic chronometers H(z), 25 points, 0.07 < z < 1.97 (Moresco et al. 2022)

sealed_predictions.statement: Given f(z) = 1/(1+z) and the EFC transition centered at z ≈ 1, the EFC background modification becomes negligible at z > 2; thus BAO/Lyα measurements at z > 2 should be consistent with ΛCDM background geometry (for the same early-universe parameters).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI Lyα and high-z BAO analyses showing significant (>2σ) background deviations from ΛCDM at z > 2 with standard early-time calibration.

kill_criteria: KC1: Using the official BOSS DR12 consensus likelihood with the full 6×6 covariance and Planck-like base parameters, the fixed-parameter EFC background returns a penalty Δχ² ≥ +5 (i.e., EFC worse than ΛCDM) or χ²_red ≥ 1.5 for 6 dof.
KC2: Independent BAO datasets with publicly released covariances (e.g., DESI anisotropic BAO) yield a cumulative geometric penalty Δχ² ≥ +9 for the fixed EFC background across z ≈ 0.3–0.8.

KC3: Cosmic chronometer compilations (with vetted systematics and covariances) show a consistent EFC over/underprediction of H(z) at z ≈ 0.5–0.7 exceeding 2σ in at least three adjacent bins and producing Δχ² ≥ +5 relative to ΛCDM.

KC4: High-redshift (z > 2) BAO/Lyα geometric measurements robustly detect a non-negligible deviation from ΛCDM background inconsistent with the EFC claim that the modification is effectively zero at z > 2.

KC5: Once growth predictions are validated, fσ8 measurements from multiple surveys (BOSS/eBOSS/DESI) produce a ≥3σ aggregate tension with the EFC background-consistent growth sector without parameter retuning.

limitations: Tests only H(z) background geometry sector
Does not constrain structure growth (fσ8 requires CLASS/CAMB validation)
No DESI anisotropic BAO (requires separate likelihood)
Cosmic chronometers use published individual errors without cross-correlations

key_conclusions: EFC background modification passes the most stringent publicly available BAO consistency test
No validated geometric channel penalises EFC relative to ΛCDM
Result is fully reproducible using standard CosmoMC/Cobaya infrastructure
Fixed-parameter test (no retuning) - pure transfer validation

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper adds a stringent, fully reproducible BAO geometry check using the official BOSS DR12 consensus likelihood with the full 6×6 covariance, showing that the fixed-parameter EFC background (DESI DR2-calibrated) incurs no penalty and modestly improves χ² over ΛCDM. It closes the prior reproducibility gap around covariance-aware BAO consistency and anchors EFC’s background modification in a standard CosmoMC/Cobaya pipeline without any parameter retuning. This strengthens the case that EFC’s late-time background is viable and shifts attention back to growth/RSD validation.
graph_insights: First explicit link between EFC and the BOSS DR12 consensus covariance node via CosmoMC/Cobaya, filling a reproducibility gap.
Bridges EFC’s modified Friedmann background to precision BAO observables and points next to DESI anisotropic BAO and Lyα high-z tests.
Strengthens the background-expansion subgraph while leaving the growth/RSD branch (fσ8) as the dominant open validation pathway.

tests_added.name: BOSS DR12 BAO consensus likelihood (full 6×6 covariance) fixed-parameter EFC vs ΛCDM
tests_added.description: Validates that the DESI DR2-calibrated, fixed-parameter EFC background passes the official BOSS DR12 BAO consensus likelihood with full covariance and does not incur a geometric penalty relative to ΛCDM.
tests_added.data_source: BOSS DR12 consensus BAO (Alam et al. 2017) via CosmoMC/Cobaya full 6×6 covariance
tests_added.prediction: No penalty relative to ΛCDM: Δχ² < +5 and χ²_red < 1.5 for 6 dof; observed Δχ² ≈ −2.4 with χ²(6) ≈ 3.4.

page_updates.new_text: Using the official BOSS DR12 consensus BAO likelihood with the full 6×6 covariance in CosmoMC/Cobaya, the fixed-parameter EFC background (DESI DR2-calibrated) achieves a modest improvement over ΛCDM (Δχ² ≈ −2.4 for 6 dof) and passes a stringent covariance-aware BAO consistency test without any parameter retuning.
page_updates.reasoning: This is the first covariance-aware, pipeline-reproducible BAO geometry validation for EFC with parameters held fixed, warranting a sealed badge on the background BAO subsection.

implicit_consequences: Background-only EFC requires no retuning to pass precision BAO with full covariance, reducing overfitting concerns.
Highest-z bin drives the improvement, reinforcing the EFC transition profile around z≈1 and motivating Lyα high-z BAO as a near-null check.
Standard CosmoMC/Cobaya integration lowers replication barriers and sets the template for DESI anisotropic BAO and joint geometry-growth pipelines.
